item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 28, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
The FCC has cited four Billings, Montana, radio stations for Emergency Alert System violations. Stations KEWF, KRPM, KYSX and KRSQ were flagged for monitoring an unauthorized EAS source, incomplete testing records and inadequate chief operator oversight. Licensee BMG Billings has 20 days to respond. Additional enforcement action remains possible.
Turning to television,
Gray Media has named Jennifer Rieffer General Manager of CBS affiliate WBTV in Charlotte, effective November 16. Rieffer previously worked at WXIX FOX19 in Cincinnati, where she helped establish broadcasting partnerships with the Bengals and Reds. Her career also includes leadership positions in Flint, Michigan, and 24 years in Lexington, Kentucky.
In radio news,
Pierre Bouvard, Chief Insights Officer of the Cumulus Media Westwood One Audio Active Group, has published a new blog challenging eight common misconceptions about AM/FM radio. The research reveals that radio reaches 86 percent of Americans weekly, more than double what advertisers believe, and attracts over 63 million listeners ages 18 to 34. The findings also highlight radio's strong advertising returns, audience reach, and dominance in vehicles. Read the full story and Bouvard's blog at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In media education news,
New research from the Missouri School of Journalism is calling for better mental health support for reporters covering traumatic events. Researchers studying journalists who covered the Uvalde school shooting and the war in Ukraine found significant gaps in newsroom support. The studies suggest that empathy, better preparation and stronger mental health resources could help journalists cope with difficult assignments.
Recognizing achievement across the media industry,
The National Religious Broadcasters has announced its 2027 Special Service and Media Award recipients. Honorees include Dr. Michael Youssef, WMCA Radio, CBN News and Moody Radio, with awards recognizing excellence in radio, television, digital media and Christian communications. Winners will be honored February 23 during the NRB International Christian Media Convention near Washington, D.C.
Turning to radio,
Hubbard Radio’s X102.3 is celebrating 25 years on the air in South Florida. The R&B station launched in October 2001 and has become a familiar voice across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast. West Palm Beach marked the milestone by proclaiming October 23 X102.3 Day and hosting a free waterfront celebration for listeners.
And finally,
The Broadcasters Foundation of America is expanding financial assistance for radio and television professionals. Its new Extended Hardship Grants help broadcasters facing reduced income, family care expenses, housing emergencies and other unexpected hardships. The program joins the Foundation's existing monthly and emergency grants. Applications are now being accepted at broadcasters foundation dot org.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
